card.title: How much of a QR code can be damaged?

body.question: A QR code gets scuffed. At the highest error-correction level, about how much of its data can be restored?
body.reveal: QR codes use Reed-Solomon error correction. Level H can theoretically restore about 30% of the codewords. In practice it depends on where the damage is, because the corner finder patterns must survive.

probes.question: What kind of error correction do QR codes use?
True or false: how well a damaged level H code scans depends on where the damage is.

claims.claim: QR codes use Reed-Solomon error correction (probe 1)
claims.quote: processed using Reed-Solomon error correction until the image can be appropriately interpreted

claims.claim: Highest level (H) can theoretically restore about 30% of codewords
claims.quote: While a Level H QR code can theoretically lose up to 30% of its total codewords and still scan
claims.note: Page lists levels L ~7%, M ~15%, Q ~25%, H (High) ~30%; H is the top listed level.

claims.claim: In practice it depends on where the damage is (probe 2: true)
claims.quote: whether a damaged code actually works in practice depends heavily on where the damage occurs

claims.claim: The corner finder patterns must survive
claims.quote: Because these elements must be read before error correction can be applied
